docs.text: @type_safe Decorator: Comprehensive Guide for LLMs ¶ version : v3.63.3 updated : January 2026 prerequisite : Familiarity with the main Type_Safe & Python Formatting Guide Why the @type_safe Decorator Exists ¶ The Problem: Python Methods Have No Runtime Type Checking ¶ Python's type hints for function parameters and return values are completely ignored at runtime . They're just documentation for static analyzers like mypy or PyCharm—Python itself never checks them: from typing import List, Dict def process_user(user_id: str, age: int, tags: List[str]) -> Dict[str, int]: # Python allows ALL of these - type hints are IGNORED pass # These all execute without error - Python doesn't care about types! process_user(12345, "not an int", [1, 2, 3]) # ✗ Wrong types everywhere process_user(None, None, None) # ✗ All None process_user({"wrong": "type"}, [], "string") # ✗ Completely wrong # Even the return type is ignored def get_count() -> int: return "not an int" # ✗ No error! Returns wrong type result = get_count() print(result + 1) # ✗ TypeError HERE, far from source This leads to: - Silent failures : Wrong types flow through your system undetected - Delayed errors : Crashes occur far from where bad data entered - Debugging nightmares : "Where did this None come from?" - Security vulnerabilities : Unchecked input reaches sensitive operations - Contract violations : Functions return wrong types, breaking callers - False confidence : Type hints suggest safety that doesn't exist The Real-World Impact ¶ # A typical bug cascade without runtime checking def fetch_user(user_id: str) -> User: # Someone passes int instead of str return db.query(f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = {user_id}") def get_user_name(user: User) -> str: return user.name # AttributeError: 'NoneType' has no attribute 'name' def format_greeting(name: str) -> str: return f"Hello, {name}!" # The call chain user_id = 12345 # ✗ Should be "12345" user = fetch_user(user_id) # SQL injection AND wrong type name = get_user_name(user) # Crashes HERE greeting = format_greeting(name) # Never reached # The error message says "NoneType has no attribute 'name'" # But the actual bug was passing int instead of str THREE calls earlier! The Solution: @type_safe Decorator ¶ The @type_safe decorator provides runtime type enforcement for both parameters and return values : from osbot_utils.type_safe.type_safe_core.decorators.type_safe import type_safe from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.domains.identifiers.Safe_Id import Safe_Id @type_safe def process_user(user_id: Safe_Id, age: int, active: bool) -> str: return f"User {user_id}, age {age}, active={active}" # Runtime validation catches errors IMMEDIATELY process_user(Safe_Id("usr-123"), 25, True) # ✓ Valid process_user("usr-123", 25, True) # ✓ Auto-converts to Safe_Id process_user(12345, 25, True) # ✗ ValueError: Expected 'Safe_Id', but got 'int' process_user(Safe_Id("usr-123"), "25", True) # ✗ ValueError: Expected 'int', but got 'str' # Return type is also validated @type_safe def get_status() -> int: return "not an int" # ✗ TypeError: return type validation failed Key Capabilities ¶ Capability Python Default @type_safe Parameter type checking ❌ None ✓ Every call Return type checking ❌ None ✓ Every non-None return Auto-conversion to Safe_* ❌ None ✓ Parameters & returns List/Dict element validation ❌ None ✓ Validates each element Optional via = None default ❌ None ✓ Full support Clear error messages ❌ Generic errors ✓ Names parameter, expected vs got Callable validation ❌ None ✓ Checks List[Callable] Collection auto-conversion ❌ None ✓ list→Type_Safe__List on return The Two-Phase Validation ¶ The @type_safe decorator validates at two critical points : @type_safe def transform(data: List[str]) -> Dict[str, int]: # ↑ ↑ # PHASE 1: Call-time PHASE 2: Return-time # - All parameters - Return value matches annotation # - Each list element - Auto-converts if needed # - Union matching - Validates constraints result = {} for item in data: result[item] = len(item) return result # Validated here! Call-Time Validation ¶ Basic Type Validation ¶ Every parameter is checked against its annotation: from osbot_utils.type_safe.type_safe_core.decorators.type_safe import type_safe from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.domains.identifiers.Safe_Id import Safe_Id @type_safe def basic_method(param: Safe_Id, number: int) -> str: return f"{param}-{number}" # Valid calls basic_method(Safe_Id("test"), 42) # ✓ Exact types basic_method("test_id", 42) # ✓ Auto-converts str to Safe_Id # Invalid calls - caught immediately basic_method(b"bytes", 42) # ✗ ValueError: Parameter 'param' expected type <class 'Safe_Id'>, but got <class 'bytes'> basic_method(Safe_Id("test"), "not_int") # ✗ ValueError: Parameter 'number' expected type <class 'int'>, but got <class 'str'> Union Types ¶ Parameters accepting multiple types use Union : from typing import Union from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.domains.identifiers.Safe_Id import Safe_Id from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.domains.identifiers.Random_Guid import Random_Guid @type_safe def handle_identifier(param: Union[Safe_Id, Random_Guid]) -> str: if isinstance(param, Safe_Id): return f"Safe_Id: {param}" return f"Random_Guid: {param}" # Either type is valid handle_identifier(Safe_Id("test")) # ✓ "Safe_Id: test" handle_identifier(Random_Guid()) # ✓ "Random_Guid: a4f3c2b1-..." # Other types rejected handle_identifier(42) # ✗ ValueError: Parameter 'param' expected one of types (Safe_Id, Random_Guid), but got <class 'int'> Optional Parameters (Using Default = None) ¶ A parameter becomes optional by setting = None as its default value - no need for Optional[T] : @type_safe def required_param(value: str) -> str: return value @type_safe def optional_param(value: str = None) -> str: # = None makes it optional return value # Required parameter rejects None required_param(None) # ✗ ValueError: Parameter 'value' is not optional but got None # Optional parameter accepts None optional_param(None) # ✓ Returns None optional_param("test") # ✓ Returns "test" Design Philosophy: Don't Use Optional[T] While Optional[T] is supported, the recommended pattern is simply param: T = None : # ✓ RECOMMENDED: Use = None default @type_safe def find_user(user_id: Safe_Id = None) -> User: if user_id is None: return None # Not found return self.repository.get(user_id) # ✗ AVOID: Optional[T] is unnecessary verbosity @type_safe def find_user(user_id: Optional[Safe_Id] = None) -> Optional[User]: # Same behavior, more typing pass Why avoid Optional ? - None is a valid response meaning "not found" or "not set" - It's the caller's responsibility to handle None appropriately - The = None default clearly signals optionality - Less verbose, same behavior Type[T] Parameters (Class Types) ¶ When a parameter expects a class (not an instance), use Type[T] : from typing import Type, Optional @type_safe def accept_class(string_class: Optional[Type[str]] = None, int_class : Optional[Type[int]] = None) -> dict: return {'string_class': string_class, 'int_class': int_class} # Pass actual classes accept_class(string_class=str) # ✓ str is Type[str] accept_class(string_class=Safe_Id) # ✓ Safe_Id is subclass of str accept_class(int_class=int) # ✓ int is Type[int] accept_class(int_class=Timestamp_Now) # ✓ Timestamp_Now is subclass of int # Wrong class hierarchies rejected accept_class(string_class=int) # ✗ ValueError: Parameter 'string_class' expected Type[str], but int is not a subclass of str accept_class(int_class=Safe_Id) # ✗ ValueError: Parameter 'int_class' expected Type[int], but Safe_Id is not a subclass of int List Element Validation ¶ List[T] validates every element , not just the list itself: from typing import List @type_safe def process_items(items: List[str]) -> int: return len(items) process_items(['a', 'b', 'c']) # ✓ All strings process_items(['a', 'b', 123]) # ✗ ValueError: List item at index 2 expected type <class 'str'>, but got <class 'int'> # ↑ Identifies WHICH element failed This is critical - Python's type hints don't catch this: # Without @type_safe - bugs slip through def unsafe_process(items: List[str]) -> int: return len(items) unsafe_process(['a', 'b', 123]) # ✗ No error! Bug continues... # With @type_safe - caught immediately @type_safe def safe_process(items: List[str]) -> int: return len(items) safe_process(['a', 'b', 123]) # ✗ Caught at index 2! List[Callable] Validation ¶ Special handling for lists of functions: from typing import List, Callable, Any @type_safe def apply_transforms(transformations: List[Callable[[Any], Any]]) -> None: pass # Valid callables def func1(x): return x def func2(x): return x * 2 apply_transforms([func1, func2]) # ✓ Functions apply_transforms([lambda x: x + 1]) # ✓ Lambdas apply_transforms([str.upper, str.lower]) # ✓ Built-in methods apply_transforms([len, abs, round]) # ✓ Built-in functions apply_transforms([]) # ✓ Empty list # Invalid items caught with index apply_transforms(["not_a_function"]) # ✗ ValueError: List item at index 0 expected callable but got <class 'str'> apply_transforms([func1, 123]) # ✗ ValueError: List item at index 1 expected callable but got <class 'int'> apply_transforms([func1, func2, None]) # ✗ ValueError: List item at index 2 expected callable but got <class 'NoneType'> # Callable class instances work too class CallableClass: def __call__(self, x): return x * 2 apply_transforms([CallableClass()]) # ✓ Has __call__ class NonCallable: pass apply_transforms([NonCallable()]) # ✗ ValueError: List item at index 0 expected callable but got <class 'NonCallable'> Complex Type_Safe Types ¶ Type_Safe classes as parameters get full validation: from osbot_utils.type_safe.Type_Safe import Type_Safe class ComplexType(Type_Safe): id : str value: int @type_safe def process_complex(data: ComplexType) -> str: return f"{data.id}-{data.value}" # Must be actual ComplexType instance obj = ComplexType(id="test", value=42) process_complex(obj) # ✓ "test-42" # Dict won't auto-convert for parameters (unlike Type_Safe class fields) process_complex({"id": "test", "value": 42}) # ✗ ValueError: Parameter 'data' expected type <class 'ComplexType'>, but got <class 'dict'> Multiple Parameters ¶ All parameters validated in order: @type_safe def multi_param(id : Safe_Id, number: int, guid : Random_Guid, text : str) -> str: return "success" # All must be valid multi_param(Safe_Id("test"), 42, Random_Guid(), "string") # ✓ # First invalid parameter triggers error multi_param(Safe_Id("test"), "not_int", Random_Guid(), "string") # ✗ ValueError: Parameter 'number' expected type <class 'int'>, but got <class 'str'> Default Values ¶ Default values work normally: @type_safe def with_defaults(param: Safe_Id = Safe_Id("default")) -> str: return str(param) with_defaults() # ✓ "default" with_defaults(Safe_Id("custom")) # ✓ "custom" Return-Time Validation ¶ Basic Return Type Validation ¶ Return values are checked against the annotation: @type_safe def return_int() -> int: return 42 # ✓ Valid @type_safe def return_wrong() -> int: return "not an int" # ✗ Checked here! return_wrong() # ✗ TypeError: Function 'return_wrong' return type validation failed: # Expected type <class 'int'>, but got <class 'str'> Type_Safe Primitive Returns ¶ Primitives are validated AND auto-converted: from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.domains.identifiers.Safe_Id import Safe_Id @type_safe def return_safe_id() -> Safe_Id: return Safe_Id("test") # ✓ Already correct type result = return_safe_id() assert type(result) is Safe_Id # String return with Safe_Id annotation - auto-converts! @type_safe def return_converted() -> Safe_Id: return "will_be_converted" # Auto-converts to Safe_Id result = return_converted() assert type(result) is Safe_Id # ✓ Converted! assert result == "will_be_converted" Return Auto-Conversion with Validation ¶ When returning a primitive that should be a Safe_ type, the decorator: 1. Converts to the Safe_ type 2. Validates constraints during conversion from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.core.Safe_UInt import Safe_UInt @type_safe def returns_safe_uint() -> Safe_UInt: return 42 # int → Safe_UInt result = returns_safe_uint() assert isinstance(result, Safe_UInt) # ✓ Converted assert result == 42 # Constraint validation happens during conversion! @type_safe def returns_negative() -> Safe_UInt: return -1 # int → Safe_UInt (fails!) returns_negative() # ✗ ValueError: Safe_UInt must be >= 0, got -1 # The Safe_UInt constraint is enforced even though we returned plain int Optional Return Types ¶ Returning None is always allowed , regardless of whether the return type includes Optional : @type_safe def might_return_none(value: str) -> str: return None # ✓ Allowed! None bypasses validation result = might_return_none("test") assert result is None # ✓ Works # This is by design: None means "not found" or "no result" # The caller is responsible for handling None appropriately Design Philosophy : Return type validation only applies to non-None values. When a function returns None , it signals "no result" and the caller must handle it. This avoids forcing unnecessary Optional[T] declarations everywhere. Union Return Types ¶ Union allows returning multiple types: from typing import Union @type_safe def return_union(which: str) -> Union[int, str]: return 42 if which == "int" else "hello" return_union("int") # ✓ 42 return_union("str") # ✓ "hello" @type_safe def return_union_wrong() -> Union[int, str]: return [] # Neither int nor str return_union_wrong() # ✗ TypeError: return type validation failed List Return Validation ¶ List[T] validates every returned element: from typing import List @type_safe def return_list() -> List[int]: return [1, 2, 3] # ✓ All ints @type_safe def return_list_wrong() -> List[int]: return [1, "two", 3] # ✗ Index 1 is str return_list_wrong() # ✗ TypeError: In Type_Safe__List: Invalid type for item: Expected 'int', but got 'str' Dict Return Validation ¶ Dict[K, V] validates all keys AND values: from typing import Dict @type_safe def return_dict() -> Dict[str, int]: return {"a": 1, "b": 2} # ✓ Valid @type_safe def return_dict_wrong_key() -> Dict[str, int]: return {1: 1, 2: 2} # ✗ Keys should be str return_dict_wrong_key() # ✗ TypeError: Expected 'str', but got 'int' @type_safe def return_dict_wrong_value() -> Dict[str, int]: return {"a": "one", "b": "two"} # ✗ Values should be int return_dict_wrong_value() # ✗ TypeError: Expected 'int', but got 'str' Inheritance Support ¶ Subclasses are valid when base class is declared: class Base(Type_Safe): name: str class Derived(Base): value: int @type_safe def return_base() -> Base: return Derived() # ✓ Derived IS-A Base result = return_base() assert isinstance(result, Base) # ✓ assert isinstance(result, Derived) # ✓ Actual type preserved Type_Safe Object Returns ¶ Full validation for Type_Safe class returns: class MyClass(Type_Safe): value: str class OtherClass(Type_Safe): number: int @type_safe def return_type_safe() -> MyClass: return MyClass(value="test") # ✓ @type_safe def return_wrong_class() -> MyClass: return OtherClass(number=42) # ✗ Wrong class return_wrong_class() # ✗ TypeError: return type validation failed Return Value Auto-Conversion ¶ The decorator automatically converts return values to Type_Safe collections when the return type annotation specifies them. This ensures type safety is maintained throughout the call chain. List → Type_Safe__List Conversion ¶ from typing import List from osbot_utils.type_safe.type_safe_core.collections.Type_Safe__List import Type_Safe__List @type_safe def get_items() -> List[str]: return ["a", "b", "c"] # Plain list result = get_items() assert type(result) is Type_Safe__List # ✓ Auto-converted! assert result.expected_type is str # ✓ Type preserved result.append(123) # ✗ TypeError! Now type-safe Set → Type_Safe__Set Conversion ¶ from typing import Set from osbot_utils.type_safe.type_safe_core.collections.Type_Safe__Set import Type_Safe__Set @type_safe def get_unique() -> Set[str]: return {"a", "b", "c"} # Plain set result = get_unique() assert type(result) is Type_Safe__Set # ✓ Auto-converted! assert result.expected_type is str result.add(123) # ✗ TypeError! Now type-safe Dict → Type_Safe__Dict Conversion ¶ from typing import Dict from osbot_utils.type_safe.type_safe_core.collections.Type_Safe__Dict import Type_Safe__Dict @type_safe def get_mapping() -> Dict[str, int]: return {"a": 1, "b": 2} # Plain dict result = get_mapping() assert type(result) is Type_Safe__Dict # ✓ Auto-converted! assert result.expected_key_type is str assert result.expected_value_type is int result["c"] = "not int" # ✗ TypeError! Now type-safe Collection Subclass Returns ¶ When returning a Type_Safe collection subclass, plain collections auto-convert: from osbot_utils.type_safe.type_safe_core.collections.Type_Safe__List import Type_Safe__List from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.domains.identifiers.Safe_Id import Safe_Id class Id_List(Type_Safe__List): expected_type = Safe_Id @type_safe def get_ids() -> Id_List: return ["id-1", "id-2", "id-3"] # Plain list with strings result = get_ids() assert type(result) is Id_List # ✓ Converted to Id_List! assert all(isinstance(x, Safe_Id) for x in result) # ✓ Elements converted! Same for Dict and Set subclasses: from osbot_utils.type_safe.type_safe_core.collections.Type_Safe__Dict import Type_Safe__Dict from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.domains.cryptography.safe_str.Safe_Str__Hash import Safe_Str__Hash class Hash_Mapping(Type_Safe__Dict): expected_key_type = Safe_Str__Hash expected_value_type = str @type_safe def get_hashes() -> Hash_Mapping: return {"abc1234567": "value1", "def1234567": "value2"} result = get_hashes() assert type(result) is Hash_Mapping # ✓ Correct subclass assert all(isinstance(k, Safe_Str__Hash) for k in result.keys()) # ✓ Keys converted Performance Optimizations ¶ Direct Execution for Simple Methods ¶ The decorator detects methods with no parameters (or only self ) and bypasses most validation overhead: @type_safe def no_params() -> str: return "fast" # ~5x overhead vs undecorated @type_safe def only_self(self) -> str: return "fast" # ~5x overhead @type_safe def with_params(a: int, b: str) -> str: return f"{a}-{b}" # Full validation (~overhead varies) The decorator pre-calculates: - has_no_params - No parameters at all - has_only_self - Only self parameter - direct_execution - Can skip argument binding How It Works ¶ # From the decorator source: has_only_self = len(type_checker.params) == 1 and type_checker.params[0] == 'self' has_no_params = len(type_checker.params) == 0 direct_execution = has_no_params or has_only_self # In the wrapper: if direct_execution: result = func(*args, **kwargs) # Skip validation overhead else: bound_args = type_checker.handle_type_safety(args, kwargs) # ... full validation path Error Messages ¶ The decorator provides clear, actionable error messages : Parameter Errors ¶ @type_safe def example(user_id: Safe_Id, count: int) -> str: return f"{user_id}-{count}" example(12345, 10) # ValueError: Parameter 'user_id' expected type <class 'Safe_Id'>, but got <class 'int'> # ↑ Names the parameter # ↑ Shows expected type # ↑ Shows actual type List Element Errors ¶ @type_safe def process(items: List[str]) -> int: return len(items) process(['a', 'b', 123, 'd']) # ValueError: List item at index 2 expected type <class 'str'>, but got <class 'int'> # ↑ Identifies which element Return Type Errors ¶ @type_safe def get_value() -> int: return "string" get_value() # TypeError: Function 'get_value' return type validation failed: # Expected type <class 'int'>, but got <class 'str'> # ↑ Names the function Optional/None Errors ¶ @type_safe def required(param: Safe_Id) -> str: return str(param) required(None) # ValueError: Parameter 'param' is not optional but got None Best Practices ¶ 1. Use @type_safe on Public API Methods ¶ class UserService(Type_Safe): @type_safe # ✓ Public API - validate def create_user(self, name: Safe_Str__Username, email: Safe_Str__Email) -> User: return self._internal_create(name, email) def _internal_create(self, name, email): # Private - can skip # ... implementation pass 2. Always Annotate Return Types ¶ # ✓ GOOD: Return type enables validation @type_safe def get_count() -> int: return self.items.count() # ✗ AVOID: No return validation @type_safe def get_count(self): # Missing -> int return self.items.count() 3. Use Safe_* Types for Parameters ¶ # ✓ GOOD: Domain-specific validation @type_safe def process_order(order_id: Safe_Id, amount: Safe_Float__Money) -> Receipt: pass # ✗ AVOID: Raw types bypass validation benefits @type_safe def process_order(order_id: str, amount: float) -> Receipt: pass 4. Let Auto-Conversion Work For You ¶ # ✓ GOOD: Return plain list, get Type_Safe__List @type_safe def get_items() -> List[Safe_Id]: return ["id-1", "id-2", "id-3"] # Auto-converts! # ✗ UNNECESSARY: Manual conversion @type_safe def get_items() -> List[Safe_Id]: result = Type_Safe__List(expected_type=Safe_Id) for id in ["id-1", "id-2", "id-3"]: result.append(Safe_Id(id)) return result # Redundant! 5. Use Type[T] for Factory Methods ¶ from typing import Type, TypeVar T = TypeVar('T', bound=Type_Safe) class Factory(Type_Safe): @type_safe def create(self, cls: Type[T], **kwargs) -> T: return cls(**kwargs) 6. Preserve Function Metadata ¶ The decorator uses @functools.wraps to preserve docstrings and signatures: @type_safe def documented_method(param: Safe_Id) -> str: """A test method with documentation.""" return str(param) # Preserved! assert "test method" in documented_method.__doc__ import inspect sig = inspect.signature(documented_method) assert 'param' in sig.parameters Common Patterns ¶ Pattern: Validated Service Methods ¶ class OrderService(Type_Safe): repository: Order_Repository @type_safe def create_order(self, customer_id : Safe_Id, items : List[OrderItem], total : Safe_Float__Money) -> Order: # All parameters validated before we get here order = Order(customer_id=customer_id, items=items, total=total) return self.repository.save(order) @type_safe def get_order(self, order_id: Safe_Id) -> Optional[Order]: return self.repository.find(order_id) @type_safe def list_orders(self, customer_id: Safe_Id, status : Optional[OrderStatus] = None) -> List[Order]: # Returns Type_Safe__List automatically return self.repository.find_by_customer(customer_id, status) Pattern: Validated Data Transformation ¶ @type_safe def transform_data(raw_input : Dict[str, Any], validators : List[Callable[[Any], bool]], output_type: Type[Type_Safe]) -> Type_Safe: """Transform raw data with validation.""" # raw_input: validated as dict # validators: each element validated as callable # output_type: validated as Type_Safe subclass for validator in validators: if not validator(raw_input): raise ValueError("Validation failed") return output_type.from_json(raw_input) Pattern: Optional Chaining with Validation ¶ @type_safe def get_user_email(user_id: Safe_Id) -> Safe_Str__Email: user = self.find_user(user_id) if user is None: return None # ✓ None always allowed on return return user.email # ✓ Validated as Safe_Str__Email Import Reference ¶ # The decorator from osbot_utils.type_safe.type_safe_core.decorators.type_safe import type_safe # Common parameter types from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.domains.identifiers.Safe_Id import Safe_Id from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.domains.identifiers.Random_Guid import Random_Guid from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.core.Safe_Str import Safe_Str from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.core.Safe_Int import Safe_Int from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.core.Safe_UInt import Safe_UInt from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.core.Safe_Float import Safe_Float # For return type auto-conversion from osbot_utils.type_safe.type_safe_core.collections.Type_Safe__List import Type_Safe__List from osbot_utils.type_safe.type_safe_core.collections.Type_Safe__Dict import Type_Safe__Dict from osbot_utils.type_safe.type_safe_core.collections.Type_Safe__Set import Type_Safe__Set # Typing imports for annotations from typing import List, Dict, Set, Union, Type, Callable, Any # Note: Optional is supported but not recommended - use `param: T = None` instead Summary Checklist ¶ When using @type_safe : [ ] Import decorator from osbot_utils.type_safe.type_safe_core.decorators.type_safe [ ] Add @type_safe above method definition [ ] Annotate ALL parameters with types [ ] Annotate return type with -> Type [ ] Use param: T = None for optional parameters (NOT Optional[T] ) [ ] Don't use Optional[T] in return types - None is always allowed [ ] Use Union[A, B] for multiple acceptable types [ ] Use List[T] to validate all elements [ ] Use Type[T] for class/type parameters [ ] Use Safe_* types for domain validation [ ] Trust auto-conversion for return values [ ] Expect clear error messages with parameter names [ ] Remember: ~5x overhead for no-param methods, more for validated params [ ] Use on public API methods, skip for private helpers if performance critical [ ] Caller handles None - it means "not found" or "no result"
docs.title: @type_safe Decorator: Comprehensive Guide for LLMs

docs.text: version : v3.63.3 updated : January 2026 prerequisite : Familiarity with the main Type_Safe & Python Formatting Guide
docs.title: @type_safe Decorator: Comprehensive Guide for LLMs

docs.text: Python's type hints for function parameters and return values are completely ignored at runtime . They're just documentation for static analyzers like mypy or PyCharm—Python itself never checks them: from typing import List, Dict def process_user(user_id: str, age: int, tags: List[str]) -> Dict[str, int]: # Python allows ALL of these - type hints are IGNORED pass # These all execute without error - Python doesn't care about types! process_user(12345, "not an int", [1, 2, 3]) # ✗ Wrong types everywhere process_user(None, None, None) # ✗ All None process_user({"wrong": "type"}, [], "string") # ✗ Completely wrong # Even the return type is ignored def get_count() -> int: return "not an int" # ✗ No error! Returns wrong type result = get_count() print(result + 1) # ✗ TypeError HERE, far from source This leads to: - Silent failures : Wrong types flow through your system undetected - Delayed errors : Crashes occur far from where bad data entered - Debugging nightmares : "Where did this None come from?" - Security vulnerabilities : Unchecked input reaches sensitive operations - Contract violations : Functions return wrong types, breaking callers - False confidence : Type hints suggest safety that doesn't exist
docs.title: The Problem: Python Methods Have No Runtime Type Checking

docs.text: # A typical bug cascade without runtime checking def fetch_user(user_id: str) -> User: # Someone passes int instead of str return db.query(f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = {user_id}") def get_user_name(user: User) -> str: return user.name # AttributeError: 'NoneType' has no attribute 'name' def format_greeting(name: str) -> str: return f"Hello, {name}!" # The call chain user_id = 12345 # ✗ Should be "12345" user = fetch_user(user_id) # SQL injection AND wrong type name = get_user_name(user) # Crashes HERE greeting = format_greeting(name) # Never reached # The error message says "NoneType has no attribute 'name'" # But the actual bug was passing int instead of str THREE calls earlier!
docs.title: The Real-World Impact

docs.text: The @type_safe decorator provides runtime type enforcement for both parameters and return values : from osbot_utils.type_safe.type_safe_core.decorators.type_safe import type_safe from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.domains.identifiers.Safe_Id import Safe_Id @type_safe def process_user(user_id: Safe_Id, age: int, active: bool) -> str: return f"User {user_id}, age {age}, active={active}" # Runtime validation catches errors IMMEDIATELY process_user(Safe_Id("usr-123"), 25, True) # ✓ Valid process_user("usr-123", 25, True) # ✓ Auto-converts to Safe_Id process_user(12345, 25, True) # ✗ ValueError: Expected 'Safe_Id', but got 'int' process_user(Safe_Id("usr-123"), "25", True) # ✗ ValueError: Expected 'int', but got 'str' # Return type is also validated @type_safe def get_status() -> int: return "not an int" # ✗ TypeError: return type validation failed
docs.title: The Solution: @type_safe Decorator

docs.text: Capability Python Default @type_safe Parameter type checking ❌ None ✓ Every call Return type checking ❌ None ✓ Every non-None return Auto-conversion to Safe_* ❌ None ✓ Parameters & returns List/Dict element validation ❌ None ✓ Validates each element Optional via = None default ❌ None ✓ Full support Clear error messages ❌ Generic errors ✓ Names parameter, expected vs got Callable validation ❌ None ✓ Checks List[Callable] Collection auto-conversion ❌ None ✓ list→Type_Safe__List on return
docs.title: Key Capabilities

docs.text: The @type_safe decorator validates at two critical points : @type_safe def transform(data: List[str]) -> Dict[str, int]: # ↑ ↑ # PHASE 1: Call-time PHASE 2: Return-time # - All parameters - Return value matches annotation # - Each list element - Auto-converts if needed # - Union matching - Validates constraints result = {} for item in data: result[item] = len(item) return result # Validated here!
docs.title: The Two-Phase Validation

docs.text: Every parameter is checked against its annotation: from osbot_utils.type_safe.type_safe_core.decorators.type_safe import type_safe from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.domains.identifiers.Safe_Id import Safe_Id @type_safe def basic_method(param: Safe_Id, number: int) -> str: return f"{param}-{number}" # Valid calls basic_method(Safe_Id("test"), 42) # ✓ Exact types basic_method("test_id", 42) # ✓ Auto-converts str to Safe_Id # Invalid calls - caught immediately basic_method(b"bytes", 42) # ✗ ValueError: Parameter 'param' expected type <class 'Safe_Id'>, but got <class 'bytes'> basic_method(Safe_Id("test"), "not_int") # ✗ ValueError: Parameter 'number' expected type <class 'int'>, but got <class 'str'>
docs.title: Basic Type Validation

docs.text: Parameters accepting multiple types use Union : from typing import Union from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.domains.identifiers.Safe_Id import Safe_Id from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.domains.identifiers.Random_Guid import Random_Guid @type_safe def handle_identifier(param: Union[Safe_Id, Random_Guid]) -> str: if isinstance(param, Safe_Id): return f"Safe_Id: {param}" return f"Random_Guid: {param}" # Either type is valid handle_identifier(Safe_Id("test")) # ✓ "Safe_Id: test" handle_identifier(Random_Guid()) # ✓ "Random_Guid: a4f3c2b1-..." # Other types rejected handle_identifier(42) # ✗ ValueError: Parameter 'param' expected one of types (Safe_Id, Random_Guid), but got <class 'int'>
docs.title: Union Types

docs.text: A parameter becomes optional by setting = None as its default value - no need for Optional[T] : @type_safe def required_param(value: str) -> str: return value @type_safe def optional_param(value: str = None) -> str: # = None makes it optional return value # Required parameter rejects None required_param(None) # ✗ ValueError: Parameter 'value' is not optional but got None # Optional parameter accepts None optional_param(None) # ✓ Returns None optional_param("test") # ✓ Returns "test" Design Philosophy: Don't Use Optional[T] While Optional[T] is supported, the recommended pattern is simply param: T = None : # ✓ RECOMMENDED: Use = None default @type_safe def find_user(user_id: Safe_Id = None) -> User: if user_id is None: return None # Not found return self.repository.get(user_id) # ✗ AVOID: Optional[T] is unnecessary verbosity @type_safe def find_user(user_id: Optional[Safe_Id] = None) -> Optional[User]: # Same behavior, more typing pass Why avoid Optional ? - None is a valid response meaning "not found" or "not set" - It's the caller's responsibility to handle None appropriately - The = None default clearly signals optionality - Less verbose, same behavior
docs.title: Optional Parameters (Using Default = None)

docs.text: When a parameter expects a class (not an instance), use Type[T] : from typing import Type, Optional @type_safe def accept_class(string_class: Optional[Type[str]] = None, int_class : Optional[Type[int]] = None) -> dict: return {'string_class': string_class, 'int_class': int_class} # Pass actual classes accept_class(string_class=str) # ✓ str is Type[str] accept_class(string_class=Safe_Id) # ✓ Safe_Id is subclass of str accept_class(int_class=int) # ✓ int is Type[int] accept_class(int_class=Timestamp_Now) # ✓ Timestamp_Now is subclass of int # Wrong class hierarchies rejected accept_class(string_class=int) # ✗ ValueError: Parameter 'string_class' expected Type[str], but int is not a subclass of str accept_class(int_class=Safe_Id) # ✗ ValueError: Parameter 'int_class' expected Type[int], but Safe_Id is not a subclass of int
docs.title: Type[T] Parameters (Class Types)

docs.text: List[T] validates every element , not just the list itself: from typing import List @type_safe def process_items(items: List[str]) -> int: return len(items) process_items(['a', 'b', 'c']) # ✓ All strings process_items(['a', 'b', 123]) # ✗ ValueError: List item at index 2 expected type <class 'str'>, but got <class 'int'> # ↑ Identifies WHICH element failed This is critical - Python's type hints don't catch this: # Without @type_safe - bugs slip through def unsafe_process(items: List[str]) -> int: return len(items) unsafe_process(['a', 'b', 123]) # ✗ No error! Bug continues... # With @type_safe - caught immediately @type_safe def safe_process(items: List[str]) -> int: return len(items) safe_process(['a', 'b', 123]) # ✗ Caught at index 2!
docs.title: List Element Validation

docs.text: Special handling for lists of functions: from typing import List, Callable, Any @type_safe def apply_transforms(transformations: List[Callable[[Any], Any]]) -> None: pass # Valid callables def func1(x): return x def func2(x): return x * 2 apply_transforms([func1, func2]) # ✓ Functions apply_transforms([lambda x: x + 1]) # ✓ Lambdas apply_transforms([str.upper, str.lower]) # ✓ Built-in methods apply_transforms([len, abs, round]) # ✓ Built-in functions apply_transforms([]) # ✓ Empty list # Invalid items caught with index apply_transforms(["not_a_function"]) # ✗ ValueError: List item at index 0 expected callable but got <class 'str'> apply_transforms([func1, 123]) # ✗ ValueError: List item at index 1 expected callable but got <class 'int'> apply_transforms([func1, func2, None]) # ✗ ValueError: List item at index 2 expected callable but got <class 'NoneType'> # Callable class instances work too class CallableClass: def __call__(self, x): return x * 2 apply_transforms([CallableClass()]) # ✓ Has __call__ class NonCallable: pass apply_transforms([NonCallable()]) # ✗ ValueError: List item at index 0 expected callable but got <class 'NonCallable'>
docs.title: List[Callable] Validation

docs.text: Type_Safe classes as parameters get full validation: from osbot_utils.type_safe.Type_Safe import Type_Safe class ComplexType(Type_Safe): id : str value: int @type_safe def process_complex(data: ComplexType) -> str: return f"{data.id}-{data.value}" # Must be actual ComplexType instance obj = ComplexType(id="test", value=42) process_complex(obj) # ✓ "test-42" # Dict won't auto-convert for parameters (unlike Type_Safe class fields) process_complex({"id": "test", "value": 42}) # ✗ ValueError: Parameter 'data' expected type <class 'ComplexType'>, but got <class 'dict'>
docs.title: Complex Type_Safe Types

docs.text: All parameters validated in order: @type_safe def multi_param(id : Safe_Id, number: int, guid : Random_Guid, text : str) -> str: return "success" # All must be valid multi_param(Safe_Id("test"), 42, Random_Guid(), "string") # ✓ # First invalid parameter triggers error multi_param(Safe_Id("test"), "not_int", Random_Guid(), "string") # ✗ ValueError: Parameter 'number' expected type <class 'int'>, but got <class 'str'>
docs.title: Multiple Parameters

docs.text: Default values work normally: @type_safe def with_defaults(param: Safe_Id = Safe_Id("default")) -> str: return str(param) with_defaults() # ✓ "default" with_defaults(Safe_Id("custom")) # ✓ "custom"
docs.title: Default Values

docs.text: Return values are checked against the annotation: @type_safe def return_int() -> int: return 42 # ✓ Valid @type_safe def return_wrong() -> int: return "not an int" # ✗ Checked here! return_wrong() # ✗ TypeError: Function 'return_wrong' return type validation failed: # Expected type <class 'int'>, but got <class 'str'>
docs.title: Basic Return Type Validation

docs.text: Primitives are validated AND auto-converted: from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.domains.identifiers.Safe_Id import Safe_Id @type_safe def return_safe_id() -> Safe_Id: return Safe_Id("test") # ✓ Already correct type result = return_safe_id() assert type(result) is Safe_Id # String return with Safe_Id annotation - auto-converts! @type_safe def return_converted() -> Safe_Id: return "will_be_converted" # Auto-converts to Safe_Id result = return_converted() assert type(result) is Safe_Id # ✓ Converted! assert result == "will_be_converted"
docs.title: Type_Safe Primitive Returns

docs.text: When returning a primitive that should be a Safe_ type, the decorator: 1. Converts to the Safe_ type 2. Validates constraints during conversion from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.core.Safe_UInt import Safe_UInt @type_safe def returns_safe_uint() -> Safe_UInt: return 42 # int → Safe_UInt result = returns_safe_uint() assert isinstance(result, Safe_UInt) # ✓ Converted assert result == 42 # Constraint validation happens during conversion! @type_safe def returns_negative() -> Safe_UInt: return -1 # int → Safe_UInt (fails!) returns_negative() # ✗ ValueError: Safe_UInt must be >= 0, got -1 # The Safe_UInt constraint is enforced even though we returned plain int
docs.title: Return Auto-Conversion with Validation

docs.text: Returning None is always allowed , regardless of whether the return type includes Optional : @type_safe def might_return_none(value: str) -> str: return None # ✓ Allowed! None bypasses validation result = might_return_none("test") assert result is None # ✓ Works # This is by design: None means "not found" or "no result" # The caller is responsible for handling None appropriately Design Philosophy : Return type validation only applies to non-None values. When a function returns None , it signals "no result" and the caller must handle it. This avoids forcing unnecessary Optional[T] declarations everywhere.
docs.title: Optional Return Types

docs.text: Union allows returning multiple types: from typing import Union @type_safe def return_union(which: str) -> Union[int, str]: return 42 if which == "int" else "hello" return_union("int") # ✓ 42 return_union("str") # ✓ "hello" @type_safe def return_union_wrong() -> Union[int, str]: return [] # Neither int nor str return_union_wrong() # ✗ TypeError: return type validation failed
docs.title: Union Return Types

docs.text: List[T] validates every returned element: from typing import List @type_safe def return_list() -> List[int]: return [1, 2, 3] # ✓ All ints @type_safe def return_list_wrong() -> List[int]: return [1, "two", 3] # ✗ Index 1 is str return_list_wrong() # ✗ TypeError: In Type_Safe__List: Invalid type for item: Expected 'int', but got 'str'
docs.title: List Return Validation

docs.text: Dict[K, V] validates all keys AND values: from typing import Dict @type_safe def return_dict() -> Dict[str, int]: return {"a": 1, "b": 2} # ✓ Valid @type_safe def return_dict_wrong_key() -> Dict[str, int]: return {1: 1, 2: 2} # ✗ Keys should be str return_dict_wrong_key() # ✗ TypeError: Expected 'str', but got 'int' @type_safe def return_dict_wrong_value() -> Dict[str, int]: return {"a": "one", "b": "two"} # ✗ Values should be int return_dict_wrong_value() # ✗ TypeError: Expected 'int', but got 'str'
docs.title: Dict Return Validation

docs.text: Subclasses are valid when base class is declared: class Base(Type_Safe): name: str class Derived(Base): value: int @type_safe def return_base() -> Base: return Derived() # ✓ Derived IS-A Base result = return_base() assert isinstance(result, Base) # ✓ assert isinstance(result, Derived) # ✓ Actual type preserved
docs.title: Inheritance Support

docs.text: Full validation for Type_Safe class returns: class MyClass(Type_Safe): value: str class OtherClass(Type_Safe): number: int @type_safe def return_type_safe() -> MyClass: return MyClass(value="test") # ✓ @type_safe def return_wrong_class() -> MyClass: return OtherClass(number=42) # ✗ Wrong class return_wrong_class() # ✗ TypeError: return type validation failed
docs.title: Type_Safe Object Returns

docs.text: The decorator automatically converts return values to Type_Safe collections when the return type annotation specifies them. This ensures type safety is maintained throughout the call chain.
docs.title: Return Value Auto-Conversion

docs.text: from typing import List from osbot_utils.type_safe.type_safe_core.collections.Type_Safe__List import Type_Safe__List @type_safe def get_items() -> List[str]: return ["a", "b", "c"] # Plain list result = get_items() assert type(result) is Type_Safe__List # ✓ Auto-converted! assert result.expected_type is str # ✓ Type preserved result.append(123) # ✗ TypeError! Now type-safe
docs.title: List → Type_Safe__List Conversion

docs.text: from typing import Set from osbot_utils.type_safe.type_safe_core.collections.Type_Safe__Set import Type_Safe__Set @type_safe def get_unique() -> Set[str]: return {"a", "b", "c"} # Plain set result = get_unique() assert type(result) is Type_Safe__Set # ✓ Auto-converted! assert result.expected_type is str result.add(123) # ✗ TypeError! Now type-safe
docs.title: Set → Type_Safe__Set Conversion

docs.text: from typing import Dict from osbot_utils.type_safe.type_safe_core.collections.Type_Safe__Dict import Type_Safe__Dict @type_safe def get_mapping() -> Dict[str, int]: return {"a": 1, "b": 2} # Plain dict result = get_mapping() assert type(result) is Type_Safe__Dict # ✓ Auto-converted! assert result.expected_key_type is str assert result.expected_value_type is int result["c"] = "not int" # ✗ TypeError! Now type-safe
docs.title: Dict → Type_Safe__Dict Conversion

docs.text: When returning a Type_Safe collection subclass, plain collections auto-convert: from osbot_utils.type_safe.type_safe_core.collections.Type_Safe__List import Type_Safe__List from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.domains.identifiers.Safe_Id import Safe_Id class Id_List(Type_Safe__List): expected_type = Safe_Id @type_safe def get_ids() -> Id_List: return ["id-1", "id-2", "id-3"] # Plain list with strings result = get_ids() assert type(result) is Id_List # ✓ Converted to Id_List! assert all(isinstance(x, Safe_Id) for x in result) # ✓ Elements converted! Same for Dict and Set subclasses: from osbot_utils.type_safe.type_safe_core.collections.Type_Safe__Dict import Type_Safe__Dict from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.domains.cryptography.safe_str.Safe_Str__Hash import Safe_Str__Hash class Hash_Mapping(Type_Safe__Dict): expected_key_type = Safe_Str__Hash expected_value_type = str @type_safe def get_hashes() -> Hash_Mapping: return {"abc1234567": "value1", "def1234567": "value2"} result = get_hashes() assert type(result) is Hash_Mapping # ✓ Correct subclass assert all(isinstance(k, Safe_Str__Hash) for k in result.keys()) # ✓ Keys converted
docs.title: Collection Subclass Returns

docs.text: The decorator detects methods with no parameters (or only self ) and bypasses most validation overhead: @type_safe def no_params() -> str: return "fast" # ~5x overhead vs undecorated @type_safe def only_self(self) -> str: return "fast" # ~5x overhead @type_safe def with_params(a: int, b: str) -> str: return f"{a}-{b}" # Full validation (~overhead varies) The decorator pre-calculates: - has_no_params - No parameters at all - has_only_self - Only self parameter - direct_execution - Can skip argument binding
docs.title: Direct Execution for Simple Methods

docs.text: # From the decorator source: has_only_self = len(type_checker.params) == 1 and type_checker.params[0] == 'self' has_no_params = len(type_checker.params) == 0 direct_execution = has_no_params or has_only_self # In the wrapper: if direct_execution: result = func(*args, **kwargs) # Skip validation overhead else: bound_args = type_checker.handle_type_safety(args, kwargs) # ... full validation path
docs.title: How It Works

docs.text: The decorator provides clear, actionable error messages :
docs.title: Error Messages

docs.text: @type_safe def example(user_id: Safe_Id, count: int) -> str: return f"{user_id}-{count}" example(12345, 10) # ValueError: Parameter 'user_id' expected type <class 'Safe_Id'>, but got <class 'int'> # ↑ Names the parameter # ↑ Shows expected type # ↑ Shows actual type
docs.title: Parameter Errors

docs.text: @type_safe def process(items: List[str]) -> int: return len(items) process(['a', 'b', 123, 'd']) # ValueError: List item at index 2 expected type <class 'str'>, but got <class 'int'> # ↑ Identifies which element
docs.title: List Element Errors

docs.text: @type_safe def get_value() -> int: return "string" get_value() # TypeError: Function 'get_value' return type validation failed: # Expected type <class 'int'>, but got <class 'str'> # ↑ Names the function
docs.title: Return Type Errors

docs.text: When using @type_safe : [ ] Import decorator from osbot_utils.type_safe.type_safe_core.decorators.type_safe [ ] Add @type_safe above method definition [ ] Annotate ALL parameters with types [ ] Annotate return type with -> Type [ ] Use param: T = None for optional parameters (NOT Optional[T] ) [ ] Don't use Optional[T] in return types - None is always allowed [ ] Use Union[A, B] for multiple acceptable types [ ] Use List[T] to validate all elements [ ] Use Type[T] for class/type parameters [ ] Use Safe_* types for domain validation [ ] Trust auto-conversion for return values [ ] Expect clear error messages with parameter names [ ] Remember: ~5x overhead for no-param methods, more for validated params [ ] Use on public API methods, skip for private helpers if performance critical [ ] Caller handles None - it means "not found" or "no result"

docs.text: Type_Safe Capabilities Guide for LLMs ¶ version : v3.63.4 updated : January 2026 related : Python Formatting & Coding Style Guide (v3.63_4__for_llms__python_formatting_guide.md) Overview ¶ Type_Safe is a runtime type checking framework for Python that enforces type constraints during execution, catching errors at assignment rather than deep in execution. Unlike Python's type hints (which are ignored at runtime), Type_Safe validates every operation, auto-initializes attributes, and provides domain-specific primitive types for common use cases like IDs, money, URLs, and file paths. Key capabilities: - Runtime type enforcement on every operation - Auto-initialization of attributes - Domain-specific safe primitives - JSON serialization with type preservation - Collection types with element validation - Enum support with automatic conversion Type_Safe Architecture ¶ Core Classes Hierarchy ¶ Type_Safe has three foundational classes that power the entire system: Type_Safe__Base - Core type checking logic Contains is_instance_of_type() method Handles type conversions with try_convert() Manages Literal, Union, Optional validation Type_Safe__Primitive - Base for safe primitive types Extends built-in types (str, int, float) Caches primitive base type in __primitive_base__ Overrides arithmetic operators to maintain type safety Provides __to_primitive__() for serialization Type_Safe - Main class for user schemas Inherits from Type_Safe__Base Provides auto-initialization Handles JSON serialization/deserialization Manages attribute type checking via __setattr__ Critical Principle: Ban Raw Primitives ¶ NEVER use raw str , int , or float in Type_Safe classes. There are very few cases where the full capabilities and range of these primitives are actually needed. Raw primitives enable entire categories of bugs and security vulnerabilities. Why Ban Raw Primitives? ¶ # ✗ NEVER DO THIS - Raw primitives are dangerous class User(Type_Safe): name : str # Can contain SQL injection, XSS, any length age : int # Can overflow, be negative, be 999999 balance: float # Floating point errors in financial calculations # ✓ ALWAYS DO THIS - Domain-specific types class User(Type_Safe): name : Safe_Str__Username # Sanitized, length-limited age : Safe_UInt__Age # 0-150 range enforced balance: Safe_Float__Money # Exact decimal arithmetic Raw primitives have caused major bugs and security issues: - String : SQL injection, XSS, buffer overflows, command injection - Integer : Overflow bugs, negative values where positive expected - Float : Financial calculation errors, precision loss Type_Safe Core Rules ¶ 1. Always Inherit from Type_Safe ¶ from osbot_utils.type_safe.Type_Safe import Type_Safe class Schema__Config(Type_Safe): # ✓ CORRECT name : Safe_Str count : Safe_UInt class Config: # ✗ WRONG - Missing Type_Safe name: Safe_Str 2. Type Annotate Everything ¶ class Schema__Config(Type_Safe): host : Safe_Str__Host # ✓ Every attribute has type port : Safe_UInt__Port ssl_enabled : bool endpoints : List[Safe_Str__Url] # ✓ Specific generic types # ✗ WRONG: # host = "localhost" # Missing annotation # items: list # Untyped collection 3. Immutable Defaults Only ¶ class Schema__Settings(Type_Safe): name : Safe_Str # ✓ Auto-initializes to '' count : Safe_UInt # ✓ Auto-initializes to 0 items : List[Safe_Str] # ✓ Auto-initializes to [] timeout : Safe_UInt = 30 # ✓ Immutable non-default value max_retries: Safe_UInt = 3 # ✓ Immutable non-default value # ✗ NEVER: # items: List[Safe_Str] = [] # Mutable default ERROR 4. Forward References = Current Class Only ¶ class Schema__Tree_Node(Type_Safe): value : Safe_Int parent : 'Schema__Tree_Node' = None # ✓ Same class # parent: 'Schema__Other_Node' # ✗ Different class 5. Simplified Default Value Assignment ¶ Type_Safe primitives auto-convert compatible values, so you don't need explicit type constructors for defaults: # ✗ VERBOSE - Unnecessary explicit construction class Schema__Ontology(Type_Safe): version : Safe_Str__Version = Safe_Str__Version('1.0.0') description : Safe_Str__Text = Safe_Str__Text('') taxonomy_ref : Taxonomy_Id = Taxonomy_Id('') # ✓ SIMPLIFIED - Auto-conversion handles it class Schema__Ontology(Type_Safe): version : Safe_Str__Version = '1.0.0' # Auto-converts to Safe_Str__Version description : Safe_Str__Text # Empty string is default anyway taxonomy_ref : Taxonomy_Id # Empty string is default anyway Key insight : Safe_Str types default to empty string '' , Safe_Int/Safe_UInt default to 0 , Safe_Float defaults to 0.0 . Only specify defaults when they differ from these. 6. Schemas Must Be Pure Data Containers ¶ CRITICAL: Schema classes should ONLY contain type annotations - NO methods, NO business logic! # ✗ WRONG - Methods in schema class Schema__Ontology(Type_Safe): ontology_id : Ontology_Id node_types : Dict__Node_Types__By_Id def valid_edge(self, source, verb, target) -> bool: # NO! Move to helper pass def get_inverse_verb(self, source, verb) -> Safe_Str: # NO! Move to helper pass # ✓ CORRECT - Schema is pure data class Schema__Ontology(Type_Safe): ontology_id : Ontology_Id node_types : Dict__Node_Types__By_Id # ✓ CORRECT - Logic in separate helper class class Ontology__Utils(Type_Safe): @type_safe def valid_edge(self, ontology : Schema__Ontology , source : Node_Type_Id , verb : Safe_Str__Ontology__Verb, target : Node_Type_Id ) -> bool: pass Rationale : Schemas capture data structure. Behavior belongs in service/helper classes. This separation enables clean serialization and maintains single responsibility. Reserved Method Names ¶ Type_Safe classes have built-in methods that cannot be used as attribute names . Using these names as attributes will cause unexpected behavior: Methods That Cannot Be Attribute Names ¶ Method Purpose Why It Conflicts json() Serialize to dict Attribute would shadow serialization from_json() Deserialize from dict Class method conflict obj() Convert to namespace Attribute would shadow method reset() Reset to defaults Attribute would shadow method print() Pretty print Attribute would shadow method # ✗ WRONG - Reserved names as attributes class Schema__Bad(Type_Safe): json : Safe_Str # Shadows json() method! from_json: Safe_Str # Shadows from_json() method! obj : Safe_Str # Shadows obj() method! # ✓ CORRECT - Use descriptive names class Schema__Good(Type_Safe): json_data : Safe_Str json_source : Safe_Str target_object: Safe_Str Complete Reserved Names List ¶ These method names are reserved and should never be used as attribute names: - json , json__compress , from_json , from_json__compressed - obj , reset , print - serialize_to_dict , update_from_kwargs - __locals__ , __kwargs__ , __default_kwargs__ , __cls_kwargs__ , __attr_names__ Method Validation with @type_safe Decorator ¶ The @type_safe decorator provides runtime type enforcement for method parameters and return values: from osbot_utils.type_safe.type_safe_core.decorators.type_safe import type_safe class Ontology__Registry(Type_Safe): cache: Dict__Ontologies__By_Id @type_safe def get(self, ontology_id: Ontology_Id) -> Schema__Ontology: return self.cache.get(ontology_id) @type_safe def register(self, ontology: Schema__Ontology) -> None: self.cache[ontology.ontology_id] = ontology @type_safe Capabilities ¶ Call-Time Validation: - Validates all parameter types at runtime - Union types: Union[Safe_Id, Random_Guid] - Optional via default: param: Safe_Id = None - List element validation: List[Safe_Str] checks each element - Callable validation: List[Callable[[Any], Any]] Return-Time Validation: - Checks return value against annotation - Auto-converts primitives to Safe_* types - Collection auto-conversion: list → Type_Safe__List Performance: - ~5x overhead for no-parameter methods - Full validation for methods with parameters - Pre-calculates optimization flags See : v3_63_3__for_llms__type_safe__decorator_guide.md for comprehensive decorator documentation. Return Values and None ¶ No Optional Return Types Needed ¶ Returning None is always allowed regardless of return type annotation: # ✗ AVOID - Optional is redundant verbosity @type_safe def get(self, ontology_id: Ontology_Id) -> Optional[Schema__Ontology]: return self.cache.get(ontology_id) # ✓ CORRECT - None is implicitly valid @type_safe def get(self, ontology_id: Ontology_Id) -> Schema__Ontology: return self.cache.get(ontology_id) # Can return None Design Philosophy : None means "not found" or "no result" - it's the caller's responsibility to handle it. This avoids verbose Optional[T] declarations everywhere. Optional Parameters Use Default = None ¶ # ✗ AVOID - Optional[T] is unnecessary @type_safe def find(self, id: Optional[Safe_Id] = None) -> Schema__User: pass # ✓ CORRECT - Default = None makes it optional @type_safe def find(self, id: Safe_Id = None) -> Schema__User: pass Type_Safe Collection Types ¶ Type_Safe provides type-safe versions of Python's built-in collections that validate on every operation : Type_Safe__List ¶ from osbot_utils.type_safe.type_safe_core.collections.Type_Safe__List import Type_Safe__List class Schema__Document(Type_Safe): items: List[Safe_Str] # Auto-creates Type_Safe__List # Direct usage safe_list = Type_Safe__List(expected_type=Safe_Str) safe_list.append("test") # ✓ Auto-converts to Safe_Str safe_list.append(123) # ✗ TypeError! Type_Safe__Dict ¶ from osbot_utils.type_safe.type_safe_core.collections.Type_Safe__Dict import Type_Safe__Dict class Schema__Inventory(Type_Safe): mapping: Dict[Safe_Id, Safe_Float__Money] # Type-safe dict # Direct usage safe_dict = Type_Safe__Dict(expected_key_type=Safe_Id, expected_value_type=Safe_Float__Money) safe_dict["ID-1"] = 99.99 # ✓ Auto-converts both safe_dict[123] = "invalid" # ✗ TypeError! Type_Safe__Set and Type_Safe__Tuple ¶ class Schema__Tags(Type_Safe): unique_ids : Set[Safe_Id] # Type-safe set coordinates: Tuple[Safe_Float, Safe_Float] # Fixed-type tuple Creating Type_Safe Collection Subclasses ¶ For reusable collection types, create subclasses with class-level type definitions. Naming Convention: Prefix with Collection Type ¶ Always prefix with Dict__ , List__ , Set__ , Tuple__ : # ✓ CORRECT - Collection type prefix class Dict__Ontologies__By_Id(Type_Safe__Dict): expected_key_type = Ontology_Id expected_value_type = Schema__Ontology class Dict__Node_Types__By_Id(Type_Safe__Dict): expected_key_type = Node_Type_Id expected_value_type = Schema__Ontology__Node_Type class List__Node_Type_Ids(Type_Safe__List): expected_type = Node_Type_Id class Set__Permission__Ids(Type_Safe__Set): expected_type = Safe_Id # ✗ WRONG - No collection type indicator class Ontologies_By_Id(Type_Safe__Dict): ... # What type is this? class Node_Type_Ids(Type_Safe__List): ... # Ambiguous Collection Subclasses Must Be Pure Type Definitions ¶ CRITICAL: No methods allowed in collection subclasses! # ✓ CORRECT - Pure type definition class Dict__Ontologies__By_Id(Type_Safe__Dict): expected_key_type = Ontology_Id expected_value_type = Schema__Ontology # ✗ WRONG - Methods in collection subclass class Dict__Ontologies__By_Id(Type_Safe__Dict): expected_key_type = Ontology_Id expected_value_type = Schema__Ontology def find_by_name(self, name: Safe_Str): # NO! Move to helper pass Using Collection Subclasses ¶ class Schema__Document(Type_Safe): hashes: Dict__Content__Hashes # Auto-initializes, enforces types # Usage doc = Schema__Document() doc.hashes['abc1234567'] = 'Content' # Key auto-converts to Safe_Str__Hash Instantiating Collection Subclasses Directly ¶ Use collection subclasses directly when building data - don't use raw {} or [] : # ✗ WRONG - Raw dict/list loses type safety def parse_ontology(self, data: dict) -> Schema__Ontology: node_types = {} # Not type-safe! # ✗ ALSO WRONG - Creating parent object just to get collection def parse_ontology(self, data: dict) -> Schema__Ontology: node_types = Schema__Ontology().node_types # Wasteful! # ✓ CORRECT - Instantiate collection subclass directly def parse_ontology(self, data: dict) -> Schema__Ontology: node_types = Dict__Node_Types__By_Id() # Direct instantiation See : v3_63_3__for_llms__type_safe__collections__subclassing_guide.md for comprehensive collection documentation. Safe_Id vs Semantic_Id Distinction ¶ Understanding when to use auto-generating IDs vs semantic identifiers is critical: Safe_Id - Auto-Generates When Empty ¶ # Safe_Id auto-generates random value when None/empty class Safe_Id(Type_Safe__Primitive, str): def __new__(cls, value=None): if value is None: value = safe_id(random_id_short(prefix='safe-id')) # Auto-generates! Use for : Instance identifiers that need unique values - Node_Id , Edge_Id , Graph_Id - Any ID that represents a unique instance Semantic_Id - Never Auto-Generates ¶ # Semantic_Id allows empty, NEVER auto-generates class Semantic_Id(Safe_Str): regex = re.compile(r'[^a-zA-Z0-9_\-.]') max_length = 128 allow_empty = True trim_whitespace = True Use for : Human-readable identifiers that have meaning - Ontology_Id , Node_Type_Id , Taxonomy_Id - Category_Id , Rule_Set_Id - Any ID that represents a concept, not an instance Key Distinction ¶ Category Behavior Use Cases Instance IDs Auto-generate via Obj_Id() Node_Id , Edge_Id , Graph_Id Semantic IDs NEVER auto-generate, allow empty Ontology_Id , Node_Type_Id , Taxonomy_Id Why it matters : Safe_Id breaks serialization round-trips because new IDs are generated on deserialization. Enum Support in Type_Safe ¶ Type_Safe has full support for Python Enums with automatic serialization/deserialization: from enum import Enum from osbot_utils.type_safe.Type_Safe import Type_Safe class Enum__LLM__Role(str, Enum): SYSTEM = "system" USER = "user" ASSISTANT = "assistant" TOOL = "tool" def __str__(self): return self.value class Schema__LLM__Message(Type_Safe): role : Enum__LLM__Role content : Safe_Str__LLM__Message__User # Automatic conversion from strings message = Schema__LLM__Message(role="user", content="Hello") print(message.role) # Enum__LLM__Role.USER # JSON serialization preserves enum values json_data = message.json() # {"role": "user", ...} restored = Schema__LLM__Message.from_json(json_data) assert restored.role == Enum__LLM__Role.USER # Enum restored! # Runtime validation message.role = "invalid" # ✗ ValueError Using Literal for Quick Enums ¶ For small, fixed sets of values, use Literal instead of creating Enum classes: from typing import Literal class Schema__Message(Type_Safe): role : Literal["assistant", "system", "user", "tool"] priority: Literal["low", "medium", "high"] = "medium" message = Schema__Message() message.role = "user" # ✓ Valid message.role = "admin" # ✗ ValueError Type_Safe Validation Framework ¶ Use Annotated types for additional constraints: from osbot_utils.type_safe.validators.Type_Safe__Validator import Validate from osbot_utils.type_safe.validators.Validator__Min import Min from osbot_utils.type_safe.validators.Validator__Max import Max from osbot_utils.type_safe.validators.Validator__One_Of import One_Of from osbot_utils.type_safe.validators.Validator__Regex import Regex class Schema__User(Type_Safe): age : Validate[Safe_UInt, Min(18), Max(100)] priority : Validate[Safe_Str, One_Of(["low", "medium", "high"])] code : Validate[Safe_Str, Regex(r'^[A-Z]{3}-\d{4}$')] Safe Primitives Reference ¶ Core String Types ¶ Type Purpose Key Features Safe_Str Base safe string max_length=512, regex filtering Safe_Str__Text General text 4KB, more chars allowed Safe_Str__Id Identifiers Alphanumeric + underscore + hyphen Domain String Types ¶ Identifiers (domains.identifiers.safe_str): - Safe_Str__Display_Name - User-facing names - Safe_Str__Key - Dictionary/config keys (allows dots) - Safe_Str__Label - Hierarchical labels (dots, colons, spaces) - Safe_Str__Namespace - Namespaced identifiers - Safe_Str__Slug - URL-friendly (lowercase, hyphens) Files (domains.files.safe_str): - Safe_Str__File__Name - Safe filenames - Safe_Str__File__Path - File paths Web (domains.web.safe_str): - Safe_Str__Url - URL validation - Safe_Str__Email - Email addresses - Safe_Str__Username - Usernames - Safe_Str__API__Parameter - API param names LLM (domains.llm.safe_str): - Safe_Str__LLM__Prompt - LLM prompts (32KB) - Safe_Str__LLM__Message__System/User/Assistant/Tool - Message types - Safe_Str__LLM__Model_Id - Model identifiers Cryptographic (domains.cryptography.safe_str): - Safe_Str__Hash - 10-char hash - Safe_Str__SHA1 - Full SHA1 (40 hex) Numeric Types ¶ Type Purpose Features Safe_Int Base integer Range validation Safe_UInt Unsigned int min_value=0 Safe_UInt__Port Network ports 0-65535 Safe_Float Base float Precision control Safe_Float__Money Currency Decimal arithmetic, 2 places Identity Types ¶ Type Behavior Safe_Id Auto-generates if None Random_Guid Always auto-generates UUID Timestamp_Now Auto-captures current time Obj_Id Unique object identifier Files and JSON Utility Usage ¶ Always use OSBot-Utils utilities instead of raw Python file/JSON handling: # ✗ WRONG - Raw Python handling import json from pathlib import Path def load_from_file(self, file_path: str): with open(file_path, 'r') as f: return json.load(f) # ✓ CORRECT - Use OSBot-Utils from osbot_utils.utils.Files import file_exists from osbot_utils.utils.Json import json_load_file from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.domains.files.safe_str.Safe_Str__File__Path import Safe_Str__File__Path def load_from_file(self, file_path: Safe_Str__File__Path) -> Schema__Config: if file_exists(file_path) is False: return None data = json_load_file(file_path) # Returns {} on error if not data: return None return Schema__Config.from_json(data) Json Utility Functions ¶ Function Purpose Returns on Error json_dumps(obj) Serialize to JSON string None json_loads(json_str) Parse JSON string {} json_load_file(path) Load JSON from file {} json_save_file(data, path) Save JSON to file - No Exceptions for Missing Resources ¶ Return None instead of raising exceptions for missing resources: # ✗ WRONG - Exceptions inside methods def load_from_file(self, file_path: Safe_Str__File__Path) -> Schema__Config: if not file_exists(file_path): raise FileNotFoundError(f"File not found: {file_path}") # ✓ CORRECT - Return None, let caller decide def load_from_file(self, file_path: Safe_Str__File__Path) -> Schema__Config: if file_exists(file_path) is False: return None Rationale : Missing file/resource is not exceptional - it's a valid state. Caller has context to decide appropriate action. No str() Casts with Type_Safe ¶ Type_Safe handles conversions automatically - never use explicit str() casts: # ✗ WRONG - Unnecessary str() cast self.cache[str(ontology.ontology_id)] = ontology # ✓ CORRECT - Type_Safe handles conversions self.cache[ontology.ontology_id] = ontology Default Values and Auto-initialization ¶ Type_Safe automatically initializes attributes based on their types: class Schema__Message(Type_Safe): content : Safe_Str # Auto: '' count : Safe_UInt # Auto: 0 price : Safe_Float__Money # Auto: 0.00 tags : List[Safe_Str] # Auto: [] (unique instance) metadata : Dict[Safe_Str__Key, Safe_Str__Text] # Auto: {} (unique instance) options : Schema__Options # Auto: Schema__Options() parent_id : Safe_Id = None # Explicitly nullable message = Schema__Message() print(message.content) # '' print(message.tags) # [] print(message.parent_id) # None Auto-Initializing Types ¶ These types generate new values on each instantiation: class Schema__Response(Type_Safe): request_id : Random_Guid # Auto-generates new GUID timestamp : Timestamp_Now # Auto-generates current time response1 = Schema__Response() response2 = Schema__Response() # response1.request_id != response2.request_id # Different values! Type_Safe Methods Reference ¶ Data Access Methods ¶ __locals__() - Instance's attribute values __kwargs__() - All attributes including defaults __default_kwargs__() - Class-level defaults __cls_kwargs__() - Class variables __attr_names__() - List of attribute names Serialization Methods ¶ json() / serialize_to_dict() - Convert to dict json__compress() - Compressed JSON with type registry from_json(data) - Deserialize from JSON from_json__compressed(data) - Deserialize compressed JSON obj() - Convert to namespace object Utility Methods ¶ reset() - Reset all attributes to defaults update_from_kwargs(**kwargs) - Update multiple attributes print() - Pretty print the object Creating Custom Safe Types ¶ Custom Safe_Str Types ¶ from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.core.Safe_Str import Safe_Str from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.core.enums.Enum__Safe_Str__Regex_Mode import Enum__Safe_Str__Regex_Mode import re class Safe_Str__Username(Safe_Str): max_length = 20 regex = re.compile(r'[^a-zA-Z0-9_]') regex_mode = Enum__Safe_Str__Regex_Mode.REPLACE allow_empty = False class Safe_Str__API_Key(Safe_Str): max_length = 32 regex = re.compile(r'^[A-Z0-9]{32}$') regex_mode = Enum__Safe_Str__Regex_Mode.MATCH strict_validation = True exact_length = True Custom Safe_Int Types ¶ from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.core.Safe_UInt import Safe_UInt class Safe_UInt__Age(Safe_UInt): min_value = 0 max_value = 150 class Safe_UInt__HTTP_Status(Safe_UInt): min_value = 100 max_value = 599 Import Reference ¶ # Core from osbot_utils.type_safe.Type_Safe import Type_Safe from osbot_utils.type_safe.type_safe_core.decorators.type_safe import type_safe # Core Primitives from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.core.Safe_Str import Safe_Str from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.core.Safe_Int import Safe_Int from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.core.Safe_UInt import Safe_UInt from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.core.Safe_Float import Safe_Float # Collections from osbot_utils.type_safe.type_safe_core.collections.Type_Safe__List import Type_Safe__List from osbot_utils.type_safe.type_safe_core.collections.Type_Safe__Dict import Type_Safe__Dict from osbot_utils.type_safe.type_safe_core.collections.Type_Safe__Set import Type_Safe__Set from osbot_utils.type_safe.type_safe_core.collections.Type_Safe__Tuple import Type_Safe__Tuple # Validators from osbot_utils.type_safe.validators.Type_Safe__Validator import Validate from osbot_utils.type_safe.validators.Validator__Min import Min from osbot_utils.type_safe.validators.Validator__Max import Max # Identifiers from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.domains.identifiers.Safe_Id import Safe_Id from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.domains.identifiers.Random_Guid import Random_Guid from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.domains.identifiers.Timestamp_Now import Timestamp_Now # Domain Types (examples) from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.domains.web.safe_str.Safe_Str__Url import Safe_Str__Url from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.domains.web.safe_str.Safe_Str__Email import Safe_Str__Email from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.domains.files.safe_str.Safe_Str__File__Path import Safe_Str__File__Path from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.domains.numerical.safe_float.Safe_Float__Money import Safe_Float__Money from osbot_utils.type_safe.primitives.domains.llm.safe_str.Safe_Str__LLM__Prompt import Safe_Str__LLM__Prompt #
